belief: I’m going to hell because of my many sins.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that you are going to hell because of your many sins, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: A long history of sin, addiction, or broken relationships. Shame that has grown over many years. Being told you were bad or hopeless as a child. Frightening teaching about hell without the good news of grace. Depression, which can make hopeless thoughts feel like facts.
teaches: Sin is real, and its wages is death. But that is not the end of the sentence: the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus. God proved His love by sending Christ to die for us while we were still sinners. Christ came into the world to save sinners, even the worst. Where sin increased, grace increased all the more. A thief dying on a cross asked Jesus to remember him, and Jesus promised him Paradise that very day. The number of your sins is not what decides your eternity; your answer to Jesus is.
self_statements: I’ve done too much; hell is where I belong.
My sins are too many to count.
God could never take someone like me.
I deserve hell, so that’s where I’m going.
errors: Making the number of your sins larger than the grace of God.
Predicting your eternal future while ignoring God’s offer.
Concluding “I feel hopeless, so I must be lost.”
Seeing yourself as “hell-bound” instead of “a sinner Jesus came to save.”
questions: What is the second half of Romans 6:23?
When did Christ die for us: after we cleaned up, or while we were still sinners?
Paul called himself the worst of sinners. What did God do with him?
What did Jesus say to the thief on the cross?
Is my eternity decided by my sin count or by my response to Jesus?
Could depression or shame be speaking louder than God’s Word?
Have I ever asked Jesus to save me? Could I do it now?
truth: I am not going to hell because of my many sins. Jesus died for sinners like me, and God offers me the free gift of eternal life in Christ. Where my sin increased, His grace increased all the more. When I trust Jesus, I am justified by His blood and saved from wrath through Him. My many sins are not greater than His grace.
hw_questions: What is the second half of Romans 6:23?
When did Christ die for us?
What did God do with Paul, the worst sinner?
What did Jesus promise the thief?
Is eternity decided by my sins or my response to Jesus?
Could I ask Jesus to save me now?
hw_truths: The gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus.
Christ died for me while I was still a sinner.
Jesus came to save sinners like me.
My many sins are not greater than His grace.
If I trust Jesus, I am saved from wrath through Him.
It is not too late to come to Jesus.
log: Each day, write one promise of God’s grace for sinners and one way I responded to Jesus.
name_example: But God proves His love for Sarah in this: While she was still a sinner, Christ died for her.
actions: Pray the thief’s prayer in your own words:
“Jesus, remember me,” and ask Him to save you, or thank Him that He has.
and write what the thief did and what Jesus promised him.
underline the second half, and carry it with you.
Talk with a pastor or Christian counselor this week.
If you ever feel hopeless or think about harming yourself, call or text 988 (in the U.S.) right away.
tracker: One promise of grace I read
prayer: Lord Jesus, I have sinned many times, but You came to save sinners like me. Help me reject the lie that I am going to hell because of my many sins. Remember me, save me, and help me receive the gift of eternal life. Thank You that Your grace is greater than all my sin. In Your name, Amen.
